title: Sayzio · Investor Pitch
speakerNotes: Open the sub-deck. Frame it for investor only — fewer slides, sharper focus.

title: Table of contents
speakerNotes: Walk the audience through the sub-deck sections.

title: Appendix · Investor pitch.
description: Twenty slides for investor conversations. Numbers are placeholders unless tagged otherwise.
speakerNotes: Shift into the investor pitch. Twenty slides — vision, market, model, traction, ask. Anything tagged 'placeholder' must be replaced with live numbers before sending this section out.

title: Investor cover
speakerNotes: Open the investor deck. State the thesis in one breath: identity-first everything platform for the creator economy. This is a Series A teaser — set expectations for figures up front.

title: Vision.
description: Replace fragmented tooling with a single identity-first platform for every creator and team.
speakerNotes: Three sentences for the vision. Identity is the new homepage. AI is the new operating system. One bill, one brand, one home. Don't elaborate; the next slides do that.

title: Problem.
speakerNotes: Land the problem in numbers. Nine tools, $214 a month, 2.4 hours lost daily, 37% of features used. Note explicitly that these are placeholder market figures until the live research is in.

title: Market.
speakerNotes: TAM / SAM / SOM. Be honest these are placeholders unless tagged otherwise — savvy investors will check. Replace with sourced figures (Statista, Gartner, internal) before sending.

title: Solution.
description: Identity, links, AI, productivity, and analytics — one platform.
speakerNotes: Three cards for the solution: surface, spine, modules. Resist the urge to go module-by-module here — the next sections do that. Land the 'one platform' shape and move on.

title: Product highlights.
speakerNotes: Tease the demo. Three moments investors remember: AskCoach grounded in your data, Smart Link wiring in one click, the cross-module funnel reveal. Five minutes total.

title: Business model.
speakerNotes: Subscriptions, AI credit packs, white-label, affiliate. Four lines of revenue, tilted toward recurring SaaS. AI credits are the wedge into top-up revenue without surprise bills.

title: Pricing tiers.
speakerNotes: Pricing tiers framed by investor narrative: acquisition (Free), highest LTV/CAC (Pro), modal price point (Studio), highest ARPA (Business). Studio is where most teams land.

title: Go-to-market.
speakerNotes: PLG + community + sales + affiliates. A distribution flywheel, not a single channel. Each one feeds the next: Link in Bio pages go viral, creators refer creators, agencies bring teams.

title: Traction (placeholders).
speakerNotes: Replace placeholders with the latest numbers before sending. Mark the slide as confidential when you do. Lead with MoM growth — investors care about velocity more than absolutes early.

title: Competitive landscape.
speakerNotes: Map ourselves against bio, links, CRM, AI. We're the only one with all four under a single identity layer. Avoid bashing competitors — frame us as the integration of their categories.

title: Moat.
speakerNotes: Four moats: identity gravity, cross-module data, network effects, workspace lock-in. Each compounds the others — that's the slide-five-minutes-later answer for the partner meeting.

title: Team.
description: Replace placeholders with founder bios and pictures.
speakerNotes: Replace founder placeholders with bios and pictures before sending. Lead with prior outcomes, not titles. Investors back people first; product second.

title: Financials & projections (placeholders).
description: Replace with the live model before sending.
speakerNotes: Walk across rows: ARR, gross margin, NRR, burn multiple. Replace with the live model before sending. Investors will pull this into their own spreadsheet — make sure it ties out.

title: Funding ask.
speakerNotes: Ask, equity, runway, post-money cap. Update with the live round structure before the meeting. Be ready to defend each number with a sentence.

title: Use of funds.
speakerNotes: 40% product, 30% GTM, 20% customer success, 10% G&A. This is a build-and-distribute round, not a fix-and-survive one. Be specific about the first three engineering hires.

title: Milestones.
description: What we'll prove with this round.
speakerNotes: Quarterly milestones for the round — what we'll prove with this money. Pricing in Q1, AI in Q2, workspaces in Q3, mobile + enterprise in Q4. Each is dated and falsifiable.

title: Exit & long-term vision.
speakerNotes: Three exit paths: strategic, growth, IPO. Don't oversell IPO — lead with credible strategic interest from adjacent platforms. Investors prefer optionality over a single bet.

title: Why now.
speakerNotes: Four reasons this works in 2026 and didn't in 2022: AI credibility across workflows, tool fatigue at all-time highs, identity becoming the homepage, mobile parity finally possible.

title: Investor close
speakerNotes: Close the investor deck. Offer the live model, customer references, and a deeper product session. Confirm the next meeting on the call before hanging up.
